newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Electronics lead Taiwan stocks to 7-yr peak close.
newsitem.headline: Electronics lead Taiwan stocks to 7-yr peak close.

text.p: Taiwan's trendsetting electronics sector surged on Saturday to lead share prices to another seven-year-high close, brokers said.
The weighted index surged as high as 9,301.69 points, a new seven-year intraday high, and ended at 9,258.63, a gain of 66.06 points or 0.72 percent.
The index has not closed higher since its 9,292.37 finish on April 30, 1990.
Turnover was a brisk T$138.5 billion.
Electronics rose 3.17 percent as local newspapers estimated many electronic shares' June sales -- to be reported by July 10 -- would hit new 1997 monthly highs, brokers said.
Chipmaker United Microelectronics was up T$3.5 to T$120.5, computer giant Acer surged T$5 to T$84.5 and computer maker First International was up the daily seven percent limit to T$107.

"Electronics' expected sales improvement again proves that the sector is the hope of Taiwan's industry, thus attracting further buying despite its recent surges," said Golden Securities research chief Albert Lin.
Brokers also attributed the rise to renewed buying by intitutional investors, especially local securities investment trust firms.
"Local securities investment trust companies, which had dumped electronics recently, entered again on Friday and Saturday to buy in the sector actively," Lin said.
Electricals also gained, as did chemicals, constructions and financials. Textiles, plastics and steels fell.
Lin said he expected a firming trend to test resistance at 9,500-9,600 next week.
